evidence.command:
. /root/thanos-objectstore.env; printf '%s
' '== available authenticated clients ==' ; command -v aws || true; command -v mc || true; printf '%s

' 'aws=not-installed'; fi; printf '%s
' '== Thanos configured bucket listing ==' ; sudo -H timeout 20s /usr/local/bin/thanos tools bucket ls --objstore.config-file=/etc/thanos/objstore.yml 2>&1 | sed -n '1,20p'
evidence.observation: The configured Thanos object-store client successfully synchronized block metadata and listed 17 objects from the bucket, establishing authenticated access through the maintained configuration.

evidence.command:
printf '%s
' '== identity ==' "node=$(hostname -s)"; printf '%s
' '== object-store services/processes ==' ; systemctl list-units --type=service --all --no-legend 2>/dev/null | grep -Ei 'minio|object|s3|prometheus|thanos' || true; ps -eo user,pid,args | grep -E '[m]inio|[o]bject|[s]3' || true; printf '%s
' '== HTTPS listener ==' ; ss -ltnp 2>/dev/null | grep ':9000 ' || true; printf '%s
' '== object-store data ==' ; sudo -H stat -c 'mode=%a owner=%U group=%G path=%n' /srv/thanos-objectstore 2>&1 || true; printf 'file_count='; sudo -H find /srv/thanos-objectstore -type f 2>/dev/null | wc -l; sudo -H find /srv/thanos-objectstore -maxdepth 4 -type f 2>/dev/null | sed -n '1,20p'; printf '%s
' '== certificate files (metadata only) ==' ; sudo -H find /etc -maxdepth 4 -type f \( -iname '*minio*' -o -iname '*object*' -o -iname '*.crt' -o -iname '*.pem' \) -printf '%m %u %g %p
' 2>/dev/null | grep -Ei 'minio|object|thanos|9000|tls|cert|ca' | sed -n '1,20p' || true
evidence.observation: MinIO was active with a certificate directory and TCP port 9000. /srv/thanos-objectstore was owned by minio, contained 124 files, and included the thanos-metrics bucket with multiple Thanos block objects and MinIO certificate files.

evidence.command: store_min_ms=$(curl -fsS --max-time 10 http://127.0.0.1:10902/api/v1/stores | jq -r '.data.store[0].minTime'); hist_sec=$((store_min_ms / 1000 + 120)); printf '%s\n' '== store-only historical query ==' "store_min_ms=$store_min_ms" "query_time=$hist_sec"; curl -fsS --max-time 20 --get --data-urlencode 'query=count by (job,instance) (up)' --data-urlencode "time=$hist_sec" --data-urlencode 'storeMatch[]={@thanos_compatibility_store_type="store"}' http://127.0.0.1:10902/api/v1/query 2>&1 | jq -c '{status,error,data:{resultType:.data.resultType,result:[.data.result[]|{metric,value}]}}' 2>&1 || true; printf '%s\n' '== store-only historical raw labels ==' ; curl -fsS --max-time 20 --get --data-urlencode 'query=up' --data-urlencode "time=$hist_sec" --data-urlencode 'storeMatch[]={@thanos_compatibility_store_type="store"}' http://127.0.0.1:10902/api/v1/query 2>&1 | jq -c '{status,error,data:{result:[.data.result[]|.metric]}}' 2>&1 || true
evidence.observation: The command derived a historical timestamp from the store metadata, but both query attempts produced jq parse errors instead of a usable Thanos API result.

limitations: Historical retrieval from the store gateway is not independently proven because the store-only query output was non-JSON/ambiguous.
The Basic Auth curl client was incompatible with the S3 endpoint's required AWS Signature V4 authentication; the configured Thanos bucket client did succeed.
